description: Seed library of mesh grammar configs for the auto-research loop. Each config becomes a render + a JSON saved alongside. The tool varies params to produce batches the AI evaluates.

DNA BRIDGE: RD coral → mesh-grammar. Gray-Scott coral heightmap becomes the starting mesh; extrude-up extends ridges into vertical coral structures.
DNA BRIDGE: RD stripes → mesh-grammar. Brain-ridge heightmap gets inset + extruded on upward faces; ridges become raised tiled ramparts.
DNA BRIDGE: RD mitosis → mesh-grammar. Self-replicating RD cells as heightmap, then bulge operation on up-facing faces — Turing dots become inflated bubble-clusters.
DNA BRIDGE: L-system plant as box-prism mesh seed. Each turtle segment becomes a thin oriented box; mesh-grammar extrudes up-facing faces to thicken branches.
Same L-system plant, bulge op on up-facing faces — branches get knobby nodes where mesh-grammar inflates the boxes.
DNA BRIDGE: Conway Life pattern as extruded-box mesh seed. Mesh-grammar then insets the top faces — blocks get classical buildings with stepped tops.
DNA BRIDGE: Life-without-Death (geological accumulation) as mesh seed. Dense mesh gets subtle surface treatment — reads as a mineral crust.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Dodecahedron from Ada primitive library + extrude on all faces. Twelve pentagonal faces each grow outward — reads as a blooming crystal.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Octahedron seed + inset + extrude. Triangular faces recess then poke through — star-like geometry.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Godot TorusMesh as seed + bulge. The donut surface bumps outward uniformly.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Cylinder seed + split_face on up-facing caps + extrude. The top and bottom discs fracture into tiled facets.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Tetrahedron + scallop edges + bulge. Simplest polyhedron gets elaborate edge decoration — from 4 faces to an ornamented form.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Bipyramid from Ada library + bulge. Two-pointed seed gets all faces inflated — becomes a lozenge.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Ada crystal + extrude on all faces. Gem-like seed becomes an exploded crystal cluster.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Diamond with inset + bulge. Jeweled seed gets recessed facets and bulged surface — reads as cut gem.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Godot CapsuleMesh + noise displacement. The pill gets organic surface texture.
PRIMITIVE-AS-SEED: Ada architectural arch + extrude. The semicircle-arch becomes a ribbed archway with visible face extensions.
UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: cylinder seed + repeated extrude/rotate/scale on the top tag. This is the cleanest transform-stack test for a readable twisting tower.
UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: crystal seed split across all faces, then the split centers are extruded outward. Uses split as a real faceting operator rather than a barely-visible cap tweak.
UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: arch seed with scalloped open boundaries and bead-caps along the rim. Intended as a decorative portal rather than a solid extrusion test.
UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: torus seed with all edges riveted. Uses edge_decorate without boundary-only mode so the whole ring becomes a bead-studded halo.
UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: icosahedron covered with scale tiles. A pinecone/artichoke test for the scale_tile operator rather than another petal-based rosette.
UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: sphere with a dense scatter of spikes and light bulging. A barnacle/urchin surface recipe using scatter instead of face extrusion.
UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: a small pedestal is extruded first, then an L-system canopy grows from the top and blossoms are scattered onto the tips. Makes the branch operator read as a whole artifact.
UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: sphere runs face-cellular automata, deletes the dead cells, then beads the new open boundaries. This directly tests CA-as-surface selector plus delete.
DNA BRIDGE + UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: Day-and-Night CA seed treated as a stepped citadel, then lightly twisted at the top. Tests a richer CA seed than Conway plus transform ops.
DNA BRIDGE + UNDERUSED-OPS PASS: a Gray-Scott delta-class sheet used as a mesh seed, then tiled with scales and dotted with beads so the RD ridges become a real ornamental surface.
FORM STUDY: pure cube podium built from repeated top-face inset then extrude. Tests whether the core grammar can produce a clean stepped base from minimal rules.
FORM STUDY: prism seed with repeated top-face extrusion and scale reduction. A baseline obelisk/tower recipe using only the most basic grammar moves.
FORM STUDY: narrow cube shaft becomes a capitalized column by sequencing extrude, inset, and one flare. Same grammar idea as the cylinder test, but on a seed that reads cleanly.
FORM STUDY: side-face selection only. Cube gets inset side panels that push outward into buttresses or ribs.
FORM STUDY: top face gets nested insets and a small central lift. More about roof/floor articulation than height.
FORM STUDY: arch seed using nothing but inset and extrude. The goal is a thicker, layered gate rather than ornament.
FORM STUDY: roof-stack on a cube mass. Extrude to a roof drum, inset the cap, then raise a smaller lantern volume from the center.
FORM STUDY: courtyard massing on a square block. Nested roof inset and keep extrusion make a compact fortress or bastion plan.
FORM STUDY: crystal seed pushed toward shrine/pavilion logic through whole-form inset/extrude. The crystal has too few true up-faces, so this version tests form-first tagging instead.
FORM STUDY: cube-based massing study using repeated roof inset + keep extrusion. More about nested hierarchy than a single tower silhouette.
SELECT-TRANSFORM-ARTICULATE PASS: top face becomes a lifted canopy by inset, rotate, then light extrusion. Tests whether transform can produce relational slip instead of only height.
SELECT-TRANSFORM-ARTICULATE PASS: arch seed first gets a global inset, then the inner band is rotated and extruded. The goal is a portal that feels shifted rather than simply thickened.
SELECT-TRANSFORM-ARTICULATE PASS: prism shaft is extruded, then the top is scaled down and inset before a small lantern is lifted out. More about narrowing and re-emergence than one continuous tower.
SELECT-TRANSFORM-ARTICULATE PASS: side faces are inset and scaled before only the transformed side cells are extruded. This aims for mass allocation by side-bias rather than symmetric top growth.
REACH PASS: top plane is inset, enlarged, then pushed farther out in two stages. The goal is a real overhang/canopy throw rather than a compact roof event.
REACH PASS: arch band is thickened into a longer projecting frame. This tests whether the portal logic survives when the extrusion gets much deeper.
REACH PASS: prism seed is pulled into a taller, thinner reach study. More about vertical extension and delayed pinch than compact towering.
REACH PASS: side faces are enlarged before a deeper outward throw. Intended as a stronger side-bias mass allocation than the earlier bastion study.
EXTREME QUEER REACH: top plane is enlarged, twisted, then thrown outward twice. The goal is not a roof but a sweeping drag-cape canopy that overreaches the body below.
EXTREME QUEER REACH: portal band is grown into a projecting wing-frame rather than a respectable arch. More camp entrance than architectural opening.
EXTREME QUEER REACH: side mass on a capsule seed is enlarged before a long outward throw. Tests whether a softer seed can hold a dramatic side-reach better than the cube bastions.
EXTREME QUEER REACH: prism is pulled tall, pinched, then reopened as a projecting fan. The point is theatrical flare after compression.
LOW-RES SPHERE EXPANSION: uses the icosahedron as the true low-res sphere seed. Every face is pushed out into a broad bloom, testing maximum radial reach before the object stops reading as one body.
LOW-RES SPHERE EXPANSION: all faces first enlarge, then extrude. This tries to make the low-res sphere feel like a crowned swollen body rather than a spiky mine.
LOW-RES SPHERE EXPANSION: the low-res sphere opens into a giant petal fan. Less body-preserving than the bloom, more about how far the spherical seed can theatrically unfold.
LOW-RES SPHERE EXPANSION: a smaller first extrusion creates a halo band, then the halo is pulled farther out. The point is layered reach from a spherical core.
EXTRUDE PASS: arch band is pushed forward in three stacked pulls. The aim is a camp portal that overprojects by extrusion alone, not just rotation or scale.
EXTRUDE PASS: cube canopy is built almost entirely by repeated outward pulls. The point is maximum overhang from stacked extrusion events.
EXTRUDE PASS: low-res sphere seed expands by repeated radial extrusion only. This tests how far the icosahedron can bloom before it turns fully into a mine.
EXTRUDE PASS: prism is pulled into a theatrical fan by stacked extrusions after an initial pinch. Less rotation, more accumulative push.
SNAKE TEST: deterministic single-face serpent grown by l-system tube segments from a low-res spherical seed. One body, no branching, small widened head at the tip.
HYDRA TEST: one trunk splitting into three serpent necks with widened tips. Minimal hydra body plan inside mesh grammar.
HYDRA TEST: broader branching crown with five small heads. Meant to read as a many-necked hydra rather than one split branch.
HYDRA TEST: taller rearing body with asymmetrical branching. Less crown, more monster lifting upward before splitting into heads.
HYDRA TEST: compact central trunk with a clustered head crown. Intended as the most mythic, crown-like hydra silhouette.

Unification proof: tag_by_grammar(flower) + paint_by_tag(flower palette) on subdivided icosahedron. Substrate's part+color channels as mesh-grammar ops. Smallest-first-cycle of MESH_GRAMMAR_UNIFICATION.md.

F-edge first cycle in pure mesh-grammar: tag flower + paint + carve sierpinski. Same flower-anatomy, sierpinski pattern carving the floor. Substrate's part+color+visibility encoded as three mesh-grammar ops.
F-edge variant: same flower, Rule 30 carving instead of Sierpinski. The CA's chaotic pattern carves through the painted anatomy.
F-edge variant: same flower, concentric rings carving. Algorithm AND anatomy both concentric — they reinforce each other.

MORPHOLOGY: tag_by_grammar(flower) + extrude_by_role drives different parts to different shapes. Petals splay outward (positive dist, scale>1), stamens spike up (large dist, narrow scale), pistil dome (small dist, scale<1), sepals curl in (negative dist). Real anatomy from one op driven by tags. + paint to colour the result.
MORPHOLOGY for insect grammar: head extrudes a rounded bump, thorax stays flat, abdomen elongates outward.
